findings.where: First screen (hero) at both widths, and the whole page: the contact action and its address are missing. The palette names an 'address strip' in pad yellow, and the texture note says the address sits at the foot of the sheet, but neither is drawn.
findings.fault: The page's one action, getting in touch with Mark, is not there. The first screen has no contact, no address (Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com) and no link. parts.txt lists no mailto or contact link anywhere on the page, so a visitor who wants to reach him has nothing to act on. The yellow 'address strip' the specimen describes was never rendered.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank or agency officer who has read Mark's line and wants to engage him would find no way to make contact and would have to search elsewhere. The founder would object too: the brief requires one direct, personal way to reach him on the first screen, with the address shown, and the personal-advisor test fails without it.

findings.fault: This control is a button that acts on the page, but it is styled as a blue underlined prose link. That is the link's reserved look, so it reads as navigation to somewhere else rather than as an action here.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who is reviewing the tile, expects a blue underline to lead elsewhere, as the article's Download link does. The same look then means two functions on one sheet.

findings.where: Palette: the Pad yellow swatch (and the Logo blue swatch's ellipse)
findings.fault: Each static swatch has a different shape. Only the yellow one has a 2 px blue edge, and the palette itself reserves blue for links and focus, so that swatch looks focused or selected even though nothing on it can be acted on.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reads the palette to learn which colour does what. A blue-edged box beside plain ones suggests a selected state or a meaning that doesn't exist, and blurs the rule the tile states, that blue means link or focus.
